ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two series resonant filters in the figure. After the input terminal of Filter 1, capacitor C1 and inductor L1 are connected in series in sequence, then connected to a resistor R to the lower common terminal, and the output V0 is taken across the resistor R. The structure of Filter 2 is the same, and the output is also taken across a resistor R of the same form; it is labeled C2 = 4C1, L2 = L1/4. Reasoning: For this kind of series RLC circuit with the output taken on R, the magnitude of the transfer function is |H(jω)| = R / sqrt(R^2 + (ωL - 1/(ωC))^2). At resonance, ωL = 1/(ωC), and the magnitude is maximum. The 3-dB half-power point satisfies |H| = 1/sqrt(2), therefore (ωL - 1/(ωC))^2 = R^2, that is, |ωL - 1/(ωC)| = R. The difference between the two half-power angular frequencies of this topology is Δω = R/L, so the bandwidth is proportional to 1/L and is not directly related to C. Therefore B1/B2 = (R/L1)/(R/L2) = L2/L1. From L2 = L1/4 in the figure, B1/B2 = 1/4 = 0.25 can be obtained.
